name: Slack
summary: The team chat that defined the category: channels, threads, huddles and a very large catalogue of integrations.

factors: Years of searchable history that the team treats as its memory
Integrations, bots and workflows wired into daily routines
Slack Connect channels shared with customers and partners
Exporting private channels and direct messages depends on your plan

export.summary: Any workspace owner can export public channels as JSON. Private channels and direct messages need a higher plan or an application to Slack, and files are exported as links rather than as files.

methods.name: Workspace export
methods.detail: Settings → Import/Export Data → Export. On Free and Pro plans it contains public channels only; Business+ and Enterprise owners can also export private channels and direct messages.

methods.name: Fetching the files
methods.detail: The export contains links to uploaded files, not the files themselves. Tools such as slack-advanced-exporter download them into the archive; do this promptly, because the links stop working once the workspace is closed.

caveats: On the free plan, history older than 90 days is hidden and older data is eventually deleted, so export before it ages out
Workflows, canvases and app configurations are not exported
Slack Connect channels belong to both organisations and export only partially
Tell people before exporting direct messages: where it is possible at all, it is also a privacy decision

paths.verdict: The least retraining: people find everything where they expect it. Read the licence note before you install.

import.summary: Mattermost's mmetl tool converts a Slack export into a bulk-import file, bringing users, channels, messages, threads and (with the files fetched) attachments. Run a trial import on a test server first.

transfers: Message history with threads and reactions
Uploaded files, once fetched into the export
lost: Huddles: free-edition calls are one-to-one only
Slack Connect channels with other organisations
Private channels and direct messages, unless your Slack plan exported them

paths.verdict: Pick it if the real problem with Slack was the noise. Expect a week of adjustment to topics.

import.summary: Zulip's official importer reads a Slack export and recreates users, channels, messages, threads, files and reactions. Slack threads become Zulip topics.

links.label: Zulip: migrating from other chat tools

transfers: Many integrations, through Zulip's Slack-compatible webhook endpoint
lost: Built-in huddles (calls open in Jitsi or BigBlueButton)
Slack Connect channels with other organisations
The familiar layout: topics are a different way of working

paths.verdict: For teams that need end-to-end encryption or federation, and have the appetite to run Matrix.

import.summary: No official importer. Community scripts can replay a Slack export into Matrix rooms with mixed results. Many teams run a Slack bridge for a few weeks instead, then archive the Slack export for reference.

transfers: Channel structure, as rooms in a space
Live conversation during the transition, through a bridge
History only partially, and only with community tooling
lost: Slack's search quality, particularly in encrypted rooms
Simple onboarding: users must learn about key backup
